title.narrative: Rapid Response to Strengthen Emergency Health Access and Mitigate the Negative Impact on Vulnerable Populations in Adel Bagrou, Amourj, Bassikounou and Timbedra, Moughataas of Hodh Chargui Region.

description.narrative: The humanitarian situation in Mauritania has worsened due to the influx of 45,000 Malian refugees and the return of 10,000 Mauritanians in 2023, bringing the total number of refugees to 238,000 in 2024. This, coupled with the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic, climate change, and regional instability, has severely strained local resources. The Hodh Chargui region faces critical challenges, including a weak health system, disease outbreaks, acute malnutrition, food insecurity, and gender-based violence. Immediate action is required to address these vulnerabilities, ensuring access to essential health services for both refugees and host populations. The World Health Organization (WHO) is requesting $ (1) million from the Central Emergency Response Fund (CERF) to respond to the urgent humanitarian challenges in Mauritania; thus, preventing excess morbidity and mortality. These funds will support the provision of life-saving health interventions in the most affected areas of Hodh Chargui (Adel Bagrou, Amourj, Bassikounou and Timbedra), aimed at preventing avoidable deaths and ensuring access to essential health services for vulnerable populations.The primary objective is supported by the following key results:1. Improved Access to Health Care: Provide health services to 49,241 vulnerable people in Bassiknou, Adel Bagrou, Amourj, and Timbedra, with a focus on women and children.2. Effective Outbreak Response: Strengthen the capacity of the Ministry of Health and local partners to detect and respond to outbreaks, such as measles and diphtheria and improve overall health system resilience.3. Infection Prevention and Control: Enhance infection prevention and control measures in health facilities, ensuring safe healthcare environments for patients and staff.4. Improved Mental Health and Psychosocial Support: Provide mental health and psychosocial services to address the needs of 5,000 refugees and host communities. The expected impact of the project is a significant reduction in preventable deaths, improved health outcomes for vulnerable populations, and enhanced resilience of the local health system to cope with future outbreaks and crises.
